title: Proverbs and sayings
description: Understand common proverbs and when speakers quote them.

blocks.text: Proverbs are quoted whole and usually without comment; speakers also allude to them by saying only the first half. Many keep old grammar or vocabulary, such as kołacz, a festive bread, in Bez pracy nie ma kołaczy. They are common in conversation and in journalism, where a headline often twists a proverb for effect, but they are out of place in official or academic writing.

blocks.translation: Every country has its own customs.

blocks.note: Literally: without work there are no festive breads.

blocks.text: Gdzie kucharek sześć, tam nie ma co jeść.
blocks.translation: Too many cooks spoil the broth.
blocks.note: Literally: where there are six cooks, there is nothing to eat.

blocks.text: Nie chwal dnia przed zachodem słońca.
blocks.translation: Don't count your chickens before they hatch.
blocks.note: Literally: do not praise the day before sunset.
Literally: what is meant to hang will not drown.

lines.speaker: Agata
lines.text: Przepraszam za spóźnienie, pociąg miał godzinę opóźnienia.
lines.translation: Sorry I am late, the train was an hour late.

lines.speaker: Bartek
lines.text: Nic się nie stało. Lepiej późno niż wcale.
lines.translation: No harm done. Better late than never.

lines.speaker: Agata
lines.text: Projekt jest już prawie gotowy, więc chyba możemy świętować.
lines.translation: The project is almost ready, so I suppose we can celebrate.

lines.speaker: Bartek
lines.text: Spokojnie. Nie chwal dnia przed zachodem słońca.
lines.translation: Easy. Don't count your chickens before they hatch.
